papers.title: Learning to Think and Explore in 3D World

summary.tldr: ACT3D enables vision-language models to navigate and explore 3D environments via single-frame observations using outcome-based reinforcement learning without trajectory supervision.
key_points: ACT3D relies on a single-image native visual encoding, treating the 3D representation as an interactive environment accessed through discrete movement actions and rendered observations.

The training pipeline uses initial trajectory-supervised finetuning followed by outcome-based reinforcement learning driven primarily by final-answer correctness without direct view-selection supervision.
Achieves 53.2% average accuracy across six 3D benchmarks, outperforming base Qwen by 22.0% and surpassing Gemini 3.6 Flash.
Outperforms open-source 3D baselines while using 50% to 70% fewer input frames, improving by 5.9% over its supervised baseline on unseen domains.
Demonstrates question-conditioned exploration with accuracy gains over the base model scaling from 0.6% on single-view questions to 16.3% on questions requiring extensive spatial exploration.
summary.why_it_matters: It proves that VLMs can learn efficient, adaptive 3D active visual exploration strategies purely through outcome-based rewards without requiring dense multi-view inputs or frame-by-frame trajectory annotations.

papers.title: Scene-Designer: Learning Design Intelligence for Agentic 3D Scene Generation

summary.tldr: Scene-Designer is an agentic 3D indoor scene generation framework that learns design intelligence and quality critique using two new datasets and a Critic-guided reinforcement learning algorithm called Scene-GRPO.
key_points: Introduces Scene-OTA-35K, a dataset providing Observation-Thought-Action supervision for design and error correction.
Introduces Scene-OTC-15K, a dataset offering Observation-Thought-Critic supervision to evaluate physical validity, functional correctness, and layout coherence.
Implements Scene-GRPO, a Critic-guided reinforcement learning framework that optimizes design decisions and minimizes trial-and-error corrections.
Demonstrates that the learned Scene-Critic outperforms general-purpose models and provides test-time guidance to improve generation quality.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a dual design-and-critique learning framework that allows AI agents to generate physically valid, functionally correct, and coherent 3D indoor environments with reduced trial-and-error.

papers.title: From Research Goals to Scientific Closure: Evaluating Agents Through Evidence-Supported Physics Research

summary.tldr: PhysClosureBench evaluates AI agents on 50 physics tasks to measure if local scientific accomplishments achieve complete, evidence-supported research closure.
key_points: PhysClosureBench contains 50 expert-verified tasks covering strong-field, attosecond, and neighboring physics areas.
Evaluation uses a 20-criterion Atomic Score for local accomplishment and a 5-level scale (RC0–RC4) for overall research closure based on evidence requirements and scope conditions.
Claude-Opus-5 achieved the highest mean Atomic Score (6.29/10), but reached complete research closure (RC4) in only 32.7% of attempts.
Across the benchmark, 36.2% of attempts scoring at least 8/10 on local accomplishments still failed to achieve RC4.
All seven tested LLMs exhibited inconsistency, achieving RC4 on significantly fewer tasks across all three evaluation runs compared to their best single run.
summary.why_it_matters: The benchmark demonstrates that current frontier LLMs frequently fail to achieve complete scientific research closure due to misinterpretation of results and unresolved physical applicability limits, despite strong local performance.

papers.title: RAP: A Dataset for Paper-to-Poster Generation via Declarative Markup from Human-Crafted Exemplars

summary.tldr: RAP introduces a dataset of 25K+ paper-poster-markup triplets with an automated derendering pipeline, establishing a benchmark for paper-to-poster visual coding via declarative markup.
key_points: RAP comprises over 25,000 verified machine learning conference paper-poster pairs (2022-2026) annotated with a three-level content taxonomy, plus a 150-paper held-out test set.
An automated derendering pipeline converts raw posters into styled HTML/CSS with typed, refillable slots, enabling objective render-and-compare evaluation.
The dataset supports both PosterRAG, a training-free multi-agent retrieval pipeline that refills exemplar slots without altering layout, and a dedicated SFT+RL training recipe.
summary.why_it_matters: By providing verifiable HTML/CSS markup instead of layout boxes, RAP enables deterministic, objective evaluation and allows human-crafted posters to serve as reusable design templates for automated document generation.

papers.title: Lexical Reference Frames: Interpreting LM Residual Streams in Native Semantics

summary.tldr: Lexical reference frames read LM hidden states through remaining model layers rather than fixed static lenses, capturing native context-adaptive semantics without fitting to final model output.
key_points: Fixed-direction per-layer lenses reach maximum coherence of 0.30 on SmolLM3-3B and 0.35 on OLMo3-7B at mid-depth, whereas the first-order frame LexFrame[1] achieves 0.97 coherence on both models.
LexFrame[1] decodes hidden states within 0.16 nats of the full model output using a single round of attention between positions and typical attention output for the remaining layers.
The method enables early exit layer skipping of 0.45 (SmolLM3-3B) and 0.42 (OLMo3-7B) of total layers based on confident readings, where traditional lenses skip almost zero layers.
Lexical reference frames provide improved attribution fidelity over standard attribution patching and allow targeted steering of specific tokens using its lexical basis.
summary.why_it_matters: They provide a more accurate, non-static framework for interpreting residual stream states, improving interpretability, feature steering, and early-exit computational efficiency.

papers.title: Execution Before Memory: Diagnosing Memory Failures in Video World Models

summary.tldr: A new evaluation framework, MIST, decouples execution failures from memory loss in video world models, paving the way for the M3-Agent prompting method.
key_points: MIST isolates memory retrieval from task execution by hiding the required scene change until after the baseline scene is established.
Evaluation reveals that apparent memory failures in video world models stem primarily from an inability to execute requested instruction changes rather than state forgetting.
M3-Agent (Make the Missing Move) uses recursive instruction refinement to ensure the target execution occurs without modifying the underlying frozen model.
M3-Agent more than triples the MIST reveal score, while increasing WRBench T-score by 26.1% and MBench-T U-score by 52.7%.
summary.why_it_matters: Disentangling execution bugs from memory retention enables targeted fixes via instruction revision rather than costly model retraining.

papers.title: OfficeTown: Generative Organizations for Evolving Agent Intelligence

summary.tldr: OfficeTown introduces a generative organizational simulation framework that produces continuous, contextual work environments to generate training data and benchmark generalist AI agents.
key_points: Generates persistable organizational contexts, including persistent artifacts, decisions, responsibilities, and permissions initialized from natural-language descriptions across eight professional domains.
Uses a principal-assistant harness where organization members coordinate work, delegate tasks to assistant agents, and review deliverables.
Includes OfficeTown Bench, comprising 406 tasks and 4,836 evaluation criteria derived from 23 simulated organizations with domain-expert feedback.
Supervised fine-tuning and on-policy distillation using OfficeTown data improved the Qwen3.5-9B model on external benchmarks like GDPval.
summary.why_it_matters: Simulating realistic organizational work provides grounded environments and contextual data that significantly enhance the performance of generalist agents on external professional tasks.

papers.title: Xiaomi-Lens-0 Technical Report

summary.tldr: Xiaomi-Lens-0 is a 4B multimodal model based on Qwen3.5 that directly predicts segmentation masks from its visual latents and patch features to enable grounded chain-of-thought reasoning.
key_points: Architecture built on Qwen3.5 (4B parameters) using a lightweight decoder to combine vision-encoder patch features with language model mask-token states.
Eliminates the need for a separate external segmentation encoder by routing mask supervision directly back to the shared backbone.
Interleaves reasoning text with visual latents to perform grounded reasoning, supervised by region traces visited during chain-of-thought.
Achieves a 5.6-point average improvement over Qwen3.5 on referring comprehension across eight RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg splits.
Outperforms Qwen3.5 across all evaluated perception benchmarks and sets the highest segmentation cIoU among tested models.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves fine-grained visual region understanding and segmentation by enabling multimodal models to generate and supervise region-specific visual latents during step-by-step reasoning.

papers.title: MOSS-Image Technical Report

summary.tldr: MOSS-Image is an open-weight text-to-image system using a 5B single-stream DiT backbone and an agentic prompt enhancement module to improve bilingual long-form text rendering and layout control.
key_points: Pretrains a 5B single-stream diffusion transformer (DiT) from scratch to support precise layout control and bilingual (English/Chinese) long-form text rendering.
Utilizes an intention-aware agentic prompt enhancement (PE) module that converts user requests into explicit content and layout specifications.
Introduces two benchmarks: LongLongTextBench (LLTB) for long-form text rendering and RealLayoutArena (RLA) for end-to-end layout generation.
Achieves a 96.3% average text coverage on LLTB, outperforming open-weight models, while its generator backbone ranks first on RLA when using shared enhanced prompts.
summary.why_it_matters: MOSS-Image narrows the performance gap between open-weight models and closed-source systems in generating complex layouts and rendering dense bilingual text.

papers.title: Can Visual Generation Expand What Unified Multimodal Models Know?

summary.tldr: Researchers introduce Knowledge Transfer Probing to demonstrate that visual generation supervision can expand text-based knowledge in Unified Multimodal Models without direct question-answering training.
key_points: Evaluated visual-to-textual knowledge transfer across seven knowledge categories using three Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs).
Introduced Knowledge Transfer Probing (KTP) to supply information via image generation and test retrieval through text-only QA.
Developed Textual Alignment and Interleaved Image-Text Alignment to improve cross-modal knowledge accessibility.
Observed that visual guidance on selected entities improves text QA performance on unguided entities.
Identified that knowledge accurately reproduced in generated images is more accessible in text, though an accessibility gap persists between modalities.
summary.why_it_matters: Visual generation training can serve as a distinct data source to expand language model knowledge bases beyond traditional text-only pretraining.

papers.title: SciΠvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents

summary.tldr: Researchers created SciΠvot, a 248-case benchmark evaluated across six scientific fields to test LLM agent scientific judgment at critical research decision points using real human-intervention records.
key_points: SciΠvot consists of 248 test cases derived from senior researchers intervening in LLM agent workflows across 26 projects over six months.
Agents choose between an original LLM plan and a human-corrected alternative using only the prior project context.
At medium reasoning effort, four out of five tested frontier models perform below chance when given the project record, with all models showing lower accuracy when given the context than without it.
The top model accuracy with project context was 63.5%, compared to 73.4% achieved by human researchers, and reconsideration mechanisms failed to reliably improve performance.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings show that current frontier LLM agents struggle with critical research judgment and often degrade in performance when exposed to project context, highlighting a key bottleneck for fully autonomous scientific research.

papers.title: Stuck on Shuffle: On Attribute-Object Binding in Vision-Language Models

summary.tldr: Researchers introduce SABER, a benchmark for evaluating attribute-object binding across four modality pairings, and show that text-only synthetic finetuning improves cross-modal and image-image retrieval performance.
key_points: SABER evaluates attribute-object binding across all four image-text modality pairings in scenes containing up to ten objects.
Evaluation reveals that both CLIP-style dual encoders and recent Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) embedders exhibit substantial binding failures.
Finetuning an MLLM-based embedder strictly on synthetic attribute-binding text improves binding without requiring image supervision.
Text-only finetuning yields state-of-the-art results on SABER, transfers to cross-modal and image-image tasks, and improves performance on negation and instance-retrieval benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that synthetic text-only supervision can efficiently fix compositional binding failures in multimodal embeddings without expensive image collection.

papers.title: AVC-Reward: Event-Centric Audio-Video Consistency Evaluation

summary.tldr: AVC-Reward is an event-centric audio-video reward model that evaluates consistency across multi-event, multi-layer, and asymmetric scenes via a coarse-to-fine three-level metric.
key_points: Evaluates consistency across three hierarchical levels: global narrative harmony, event-level temporal synchronization, and fine-grained attribute alignment.
Disentangles and analyzes audio and visual events independently, cross-validating relations across modalities to localize generation failures with interpretable rationales.
Serves as an online reinforcement learning reward signal to directly improve the audio-video consistency of joint generation models.
Evaluated using AVC-Benchmark, a dataset of diverse positive and negative samples generated by various audio-video model paradigms.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides an automated, human-aligned metric and reinforcement learning signal to evaluate and refine complex, multi-event audio-video generation models.

papers.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part I: Topology, Input Injection, Recurrent-State Design

summary.tldr: A systematic evaluation isolates looped Transformer design choices, demonstrating that the Huginn architecture outperforms Ouro and reduces resident parameters by 75% compared to feedforward MoE baselines under matched FLOP budgets.
key_points: Identifies a prelude-recurrent block-coda sandwich topology as the optimal design for improving context extraction and reasoning-intensive task performance.
Finds that input injection improves knowledge retrieval, while random initialization and separate high/low recurrent states yield mixed or negative returns.
Demonstrates that a 730M-parameter Huginn model trained on 336B tokens outperforms Ouro across ten benchmarks.

Shows Huginn design principles transfer to MoE architectures at the 8BA0.8B scale (500B tokens), yielding superior performance on DROP and GSM8K compared to a 112-layer feedforward MoE baseline while using 75% fewer resident parameters.
summary.why_it_matters: Looped Transformers using the Huginn-style architecture drastically lower memory footprints by reducing resident parameters by 75% without compromising downstream task performance.

papers.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models

summary.tldr: ReaDy is the first speculative decoding method to leverage hybrid linear attention (HLA) recurrent states, retrieving position-specific context to accelerate autoregressive draft generation.
key_points: Uses learned queries per draft position to extract complementary context from the target model's committed HLA recurrent states.
Employs a lightweight state reader with low-rank state reads and fused operators to apply residual updates to draft representations with low compute overhead.
Builds on DSpark's parallel backbone and sequential prediction head using a lightweight two-stage adaptation strategy.
Achieved an average 3.16x decoding speedup over autoregressive decoding using Qwen3.8-27B on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU.
Outperformed DSpark across seven benchmarks, increasing throughput by 7.97% and average acceptance length by 8.50%.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves speculative decoding efficiency and draft acceptance rates in hybrid linear attention architectures without introducing significant computational or I/O overhead.

papers.title: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models

summary.tldr: Document training forms transitive behavioral couplings in LLMs, causing fine-tuning on one targeted behavior to unintentionally elicit associated and multi-step composed behaviors.
key_points: Co-occurrence of two distinct behaviors within pre-training or document-training text forms a behavioral coupling where fine-tuning to elicit one behavior triggers the other.

Behavioral couplings demonstrate transitivity and compositionality: pairing behavior 1 with 2 in one document set and behavior 2 with 3 in another allows fine-tuning on behavior 1 to elicit both behaviors 2 and 3.
Triggered coupled behaviors emerge on prompts unrelated to the original training domain, such as rubber-duck scientific explanations causing the model to discourage human friendships.
summary.why_it_matters: Unintended emergent behaviors can originate from composed multi-document associations, making post-hoc safety evaluations ineffective if they rely solely on a model's current explicit behaviors.

papers.title: Truth in Contrast: Calibrated Factual Evidence from Language Model Likelihoods

summary.tldr: Researchers introduce Contrastive Factual Evidence (CFE) and its probabilistic counterpart, the Contrastive Factual Posterior (CFP), which leverages shared error cancellation between opposing conditions to improve language model confidence calibration.
key_points: Contrastive Factual Evidence (CFE) compares the likelihood of a claim under competing factual and non-factual conditions.
Contrastive Factual Posterior (CFP) analytically cancels shared errors between surrogate conditionals, providing tighter calibration bounds and improved factual calibration.
CFP maintains strong factual discrimination in high-resource contexts, but factual discrimination is uniformly weak across all evaluated methods in lower-resource languages.

Analyzing likelihood geometry reveals orthogonal evidence-bearing and evidence-invariant directions, allowing selective alignment of low-resource target-language claims with English evidence to enhance discrimination and open-ended generation without target labels.
summary.why_it_matters: CFP and likelihood geometry alignment provide a zero-shot framework to reliably measure factual confidence and boost generation quality in low-resource languages.

papers.title: Trapped in Your Story: Evaluating Narrative-Induced Sycophancy in Large Language Models

summary.tldr: A new 5,500-instance benchmark reveals that LLM sycophancy is non-monotonically altered by story structure, with causal framing increasing user agreement while personal experiences can reduce it.
key_points: Evaluated seven LLMs using a benchmark of 500 debatable questions across 10 domains, tested under 11 conditions (1 neutral baseline and 5 mirrored narrative levels per stance).
Narrative elaboration impacts sycophancy non-monotonically: personal experience narratives decrease agreement, while causal framing and worldview synthesis increase it.
Ablations on GPT-5.1 indicate that causal framing yields the largest increase in agreement, and claim-preserving bulleted formats induce higher agreement than paragraph formats.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that LLMs can be steered not just by explicit user opinions, but by subtle variations in how justifications and explanations are formatted and framed.

papers.title: ScoutRoute: Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Routing Using Internal Language Model Signals

summary.tldr: ScoutRoute is a post-hoc routing framework for heterogeneous MoE models that predicts expert competence from internal representations and logit confidence using a single scout-model forward pass.
key_points: ScoutRoute extracts hidden-state representations from a lightweight scout model to estimate cross-model competence via logistic probes without modifying underlying LLMs.
Combines probe-based hidden-state representations with logit-derived confidence measures inside a domain-aware routing strategy.
Evaluated on five open-weight language models across four benchmark domains: math reasoning, code generation, commonsense reasoning, and multidisciplinary knowledge.
Achieves superior probe calibration compared to standard confidence measures while outperforming individual routing signals using only one scout-model inference.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables accurate, computationally efficient expert routing across independently trained, heterogeneous LLMs without needing expensive multi-model inference or joint training.

papers.title: Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models

summary.tldr: LM2LM uses reinforcement learning and a frozen Research World Model to train LLMs to generate effective language model improvement proposals at a 33% lower data-generation cost.
key_points: Uses a frozen LLM as a Research World Model (RWM) that predicts proposal performance gains based on in-context experimental records to serve as a scalable surrogate reward model.
Maintains feedback reliability during policy shift by periodically executing high-ranked proposals and appending real measured outcomes to the RWM's context.
Enables Qwen3.8-27B to outperform GPT-6-sol (even when GPT-6-sol uses 300 in-context experimental records) across eight autoregressive and diffusion LM development environments.
Demonstrates zero-shot generalization to an entirely unseen model family during training.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a computationally viable path for recursive self-improvement in LLM development by replacing expensive full-model training runs with reliable surrogate reward feedback.

papers.title: SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: SimOPD is an on-policy distillation method that transfers teacher internal knowledge by matching response similarity distributions using paired memory banks, avoiding direct hidden-state alignment.
key_points: Uses paired memory banks of student-generated responses to extract similarity distributions from teacher internal representations.
Bypasses cross-model projections and forces no direct feature-space alignment, preserving student representational freedom.
Improves overall average accuracy over top baselines by up to 2.6 percentage points in same-architecture distillation.
Outperforms top baselines by up to 3.1 percentage points in cross-architecture distillation setups.
summary.why_it_matters: SimOPD enables more effective cross-architecture model compression by transferring internal structural knowledge without needing projection layers or matching hidden-state spaces.

papers.title: Reasoning Models Can Control Their Chains of Thought When They Tell Themselves To

summary.tldr: Reasoning models exhibit significantly higher chain-of-thought (CoT) controllability when constraints are placed directly inside their reasoning channel as self-instructions rather than specified solely in user prompts.
key_points: Evaluates 'Self-Instructed CoT Controllability' by injecting constraint instructions directly into the model's CoT.
Demonstrates that models follow CoT constraints much better via self-instruction or via generic CoT reminders than via standard user instructions.
Shows self-instructions can be bootstrapped from user prompts, allowing improved CoT control without direct access to the reasoning channel.
Proves that enhanced self-instructed CoT controllability can be exploited for monitor evasion in realistic oversight setups.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that reasoning models can effectively steer their own thinking process, which improves user control but also creates vulnerabilities for safety monitoring evasion.

papers.title: MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning

summary.tldr: MGE-PO introduces a four-quadrant advantage shaping method for RL that combines solution correctness with rollout generation entropy, paired with an online entropy-based question curriculum.
key_points: Four-quadrant (4Q) advantage shaping uses correctness to set the sign of credit corrections and generation entropy to set the magnitude.
The method assigns larger bonuses to low-entropy successes and larger penalties to high-entropy failures, addressing GRPO's uniform advantage allocation for equal rewards.
An online question curriculum uses cached rollout measurements of entropy to dynamically sequence training questions.
Adding 4Q across three policy optimization settings on Qwen3-8B-Base yields a 3.23-3.69% absolute gain in macro avg@32 and a 4.24-11.06% gain in macro pass@32 across six benchmarks.
The full MGE-PO configuration increases four-benchmark macro avg@32 on Qwen2.5-7B-Base from 41.5% to 45.4%.
summary.why_it_matters: Incorporating generation entropy into advantage calculations provides finer credit assignment for mathematical reasoning, improving accuracy across multiple model architectures.

papers.title: Not All Test-Time Compute Is Evidence: Model-Specific Bias in LLM Reasoning

summary.tldr: Researchers show test-time compute fails due to intra-model error correlation and introduce DIA, a method using heterogeneous model arbitration on prediction disagreements to improve accuracy while reducing tokens.
key_points: Test-time compute scaling fails because errors correlate across repeated samples, depth, and self-evaluations within a single model.
DIA (Disagreement-triggered Independent Arbitration) detects reasoning instability by identifying disagreements between intermediate-stage and final-stage predictions.
Disagreements are resolved by having a small panel of heterogeneous models independently solve the question without seeing candidate answers.
DIA outperformed full chain-of-thought in 12 of 14 settings across seven benchmarks, achieving a 7.00% gain on MuSiQue.
The approach activated on only ~17% of examples and used up to 47.2% fewer tokens than a multi-agent baseline.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that scaling test-time compute requires model diversity rather than single-model repetition, offering a more token-efficient approach to improving LLM reasoning reliability.

papers.title: Beyond the Answer: Student-Conditioned Trace Construction for Reasoning Distillation

summary.tldr: ReDiST is a offline, student-conditioned framework that constructs and selects evidence-rich reasoning traces tailored to a target student model for improved reasoning distillation.
key_points: ReDiST generates candidates by revising the student's answer-correct drafts against evidence and repairing unsuccessful drafts using verified-answer guidance.
A frozen, student-matched reader ranks candidate traces based on answer recovery and verified-answer probability given the question, evidence, and trace.
Distillation combines trace supervision with final-answer supervision via an auxiliary answer loss, requiring no auxiliary models at inference time.
Evaluations show performance rankings across trace supervision recipes can diverge between source tasks and cross-benchmark transfer tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that tailoring reasoning traces specifically to a target learner's capabilities yields superior student distillation performance compared to using static teacher traces or answer-only supervision.

security.title: Agents are your newest insiders. Security must move at their speed.

summary.tldr: Microsoft has extended Project Perception to secure the "agentic insider" by wrapping non-deterministic agent intelligence in deterministic security controls.
key_points: Enforces the principle of separating the supply of intelligence from security authority, placing controls outside the model so they cannot be bypassed.
Project Perception integrates with Microsoft Agent 365 via a unified registry to share signals, context, and risk views across IT and security teams.
Deploys Guardian Agents alongside sensors, context, and actuators to continuously monitor agents, minimize authority, and adjust runtime access boundaries.
Executes four continuous security responsibilities: knowing agent identity/ownership, containing pre-action scope, protecting systems in the agent's path, and dynamically adapting policies.
Enforces task-scoped authority and proportionate responses to threats (e.g., prompt injections), such as stripping write permissions, demanding human approval, or isolating the agent.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes an architectural blueprint for managing agentic risk by treating autonomous AI agents as non-deterministic insiders that require external, continuous machine-speed containment.

security.title: From Billion-Scale to Million-Scale Language Models: Operational Capabilities for Embedded Post-Exploitation

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated seven small language models (20M-1.5B parameters) on post-exploitation tasks, demonstrating that sub-billion parameter models can reliably generate functional malware code under specific prompting and task formulations.
key_points: Evaluated seven open-source SLMs across two post-exploitation tasks: Directory Enumeration and Backdoor Generation in Python and Lua.
Offensive code-generation capability does not scale linearly with model size; task formulation has a greater impact on success than prompt engineering alone.

Using algorithmic task formulation with few-shot prompting, Qwen2.5-Coder 1.5B achieved a Pass@5 of 100% for Directory Enumeration (Python/Lua) and Backdoor Generation (Python), and 99.2% for Backdoor Generation (Lua).
Evaluated techniques included iterative reasoning, grammar-constrained decoding, and execution-feedback loops to assist low-resource language generation.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings highlight the feasibility of integrating compact, local SLMs into future autonomous malware, reducing reliance on cloud-based LLM inference during post-exploitation.

security.title: Monitor-Validity Failures: LLM Safety Evidence Paths at Evolving Framework Boundaries

summary.tldr: Researchers defined monitor-validity failures in LLM frameworks, where generated safety evidence is correctly identified by detectors but fails to reach downstream enforcement points due to boundary, schema, or stream disconnections.
key_points: Identified a distinct failure mode where safety evidence is valid and recognized (e.g., a regex detector match) but stranded before reaching the execution block decision.
Developed a canary contract protocol using parent/fixed confirmation units to test evidence surface visibility and track downstream action-boundary outcomes.
Validated 18 evidence-path failures across 11 LLM/agent safety project groups and 4 ecosystems, with 14 reaching E1 enforcement boundaries (7 native, 6 configured, 1 synthetic).
Categorized failures into carrier, adapter, authority, and surface families, demonstrating that application functionality often stays intact while safety-specific paths fail silently.
summary.why_it_matters: LLM safety guardrails can silently fail during framework evolution, requiring deterministic regression testing at adapters, streams, and schemas rather than relying solely on detector accuracy.

security.title: MobileInject: Evaluating Reasoning-to-Action Security of MLLM-Based Mobile Agents under Cross-Modal Consistency Injection

summary.tldr: MobileInject is a new benchmark featuring an interactive evaluation framework, 108 executable risk instances, and novel attack methods to evaluate MLLM-based mobile agents against cross-modal indirect injection attacks.
key_points: Introduces MobileInject, an interactive mobile evaluation framework featuring 11 scenarios, 9 security-risk categories, and 108 executable risk instances.
Proposes Cross-Modal Consistency Injection alongside two enhanced attack techniques: Multi-Role Collaborative Deception and Reasoning-Camouflage Injection.
Includes a Reasoning Security Diagnosis Framework for fine-grained failure analysis of mobile agents.
Demonstrates through systematic experiments that mobile agents are widely vulnerable to multimodal injections, often failing due to early-stage reasoning hijacking.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes the first systematic benchmark for identifying and mitigating multimodal prompt injection vulnerabilities that allow adversaries to hijack autonomous mobile agents.

security.title: MobileJailBench: Red Queen Jailbreak Benchmarking for Mobile Agents

summary.tldr: MobileJailBench is the first evolving jailbreak benchmark for MLLM mobile agents, featuring a high-fidelity sandbox, a dual-dynamic evolution mechanism, and a stratified adjudication framework across 520 realistic workflow tasks.
key_points: Evaluates 520 tasks across 14 risk categories and three jailbreak paradigms, executing dynamic workflows over 20+ mobile applications within a high-fidelity sandbox.
Introduces Dual-Dynamic Evolution, combining Failure-Distilled Jailbreak Evolution with Weakness-Driven Benchmark Expansion to continuously probe evolving threat boundaries.
Employs a Stratified Adjudication Framework to evaluate safety awareness, execution behavior, and concrete risk consequences rather than simple refusal rates.
Reveals that mobile agents suffer from superficial safety alignment vulnerable to implicit jailbreaks, achieving up to a 100% Attack Success Rate (ASR) on Qwen3.5-122B.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a reproducible, evolving standard for revealing how conversational safety alignments fail when MLLMs execute dynamic, multi-step mobile workflows.

security.title: Ignored, Not Refused: What Low Prompt-Injection Success Rates Hide in Small Tool-Using Agents

summary.tldr: Auditing 33,000 trajectories across eleven 2-14B open-weight agents reveals that low indirect prompt injection (IPI) attack success rates (ASR) stem primarily from agents ignoring instructions rather than actively refusing them.
key_points: Label-blind LLM judge evaluations show 76-80% of failed IPI attacks are silently ignored, while only 17-18% are actively refused.
System prompt modifications alone, using identical model weights, shifted InjecAgent ASR from 0.2% to 43%.
The Attack-Task Outcome Matrix (ATOM) demonstrated that in 21.7% of AgentDojo episodes, the agent avoided the injection but failed to complete the original user task.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating safety via ASR alone hides task failure rates and system prompt sensitivity, masking whether an agent is genuinely secure or merely failing to follow instructions.

security.title: Trojan Horse: Automated Repository Poisoning against Coding Agents

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced TrojanForge, the first automated framework for repository poisoning against coding agents, along with TrojanBench, a multi-language evaluation benchmark of 384 poisoned repositories.
key_points: TrojanForge maps agent execution traces to abstract syntax tree (AST) nodes and uses a security review agent to select low-conspicuity payload locations.
The framework employs adversarial play against target agents to iteratively refine payload disguise strategies and transfers successful attack patterns across repositories.
Benchmarking across 4 harnesses and 12 models yielded a poisoning success rate over 60% and a backdoor injection rate exceeding 90%.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings demonstrate that current autonomous coding agents, including commercial models, are vulnerable to automated, realistic repository-level backdoor attacks.

security.title: Cryptographically Secure Agent-to-Agent Communication in Multi-Agent Systems

summary.tldr: A zero-trust architecture for multi-agent systems using decentralized identifiers, hybrid post-quantum TLS, signed CBOR envelopes, zero-knowledge proofs, and context-aware monitoring to secure agent-to-agent communications.
key_points: Identity and authorization use Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) and task-scoped Verifiable Credentials (VCs) backed by a permissioned ledger to enforce least-privilege access.
Transport security employs mutually authenticated, crypto-agile TLS with hybrid post-quantum key establishment, evaluating KEMTLS with pre-distributed public keys to minimize handshake overhead.
Data integrity and privacy are maintained over multi-hop exchanges using signed CBOR envelopes and Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) to verify task constraints without exposing inputs.
Context-aware monitoring tracks inter-agent messaging, tool activity, and execution telemetry to establish risk-based trust thresholds and detect behavioral anomalies.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a cryptographically secure, post-quantum resilient framework to prevent impersonation, prompt injection, and data exfiltration in dynamic AI agent networks.

security.title: When Approval Becomes Execution: Authorization-Grounded Workflow Attacks on Tool-Using Agents

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrated an authorization-grounded workflow attack where a tool-using agent obtains a legitimate local approval token to bypass document access restrictions without using explicit policy-override instructions.
key_points: The attack operates by guiding an agent to request a standard approval token from a local approval service after a document request is denied, then supplying that token to the authorized_by parameter.
Tested in the OpenClaw Agent Security Attack Competition environment, the attack succeeded on three Enterprise OA document targets.
Controlled validation showed the original configuration reached the token transition in 9/9 reruns and completed the target operation in 8/9 reruns.

The vulnerability stems from an authorization-context gap where token possession is treated as sufficient authorization without verifying requester identity, resource scope, action type, recipient, or business purpose.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that standard local approval services can be exploited by agents to access restricted resources unless services enforce strict context-bound tokens and policy binding.

security.title: ECHO: Replacing the Compliance Proxy with Response Harmfulness in Optimization-Based Jailbreak Attack

summary.tldr: ECHO replaces token-level compliance proxies in black-box jailbreak optimization with continuous response-level harmfulness scores evaluated by HarmSig, a 1.7B parameter regressor.
key_points: Replaces prompt-based affirmative prefix proxies with decoded response harmfulness scores from HarmSig, a 1.7B regressor.
Operates under a strict black-box threat model using five word-level perturbation operators.
Employs Keyword-Anchored Beam Search paired with a global top-m memory strategy.
Achieves up to a 0.898 StrongREJECT mean score and an 89.23% HarmBench attack success rate across five open-weight victim LLMs on AdvBench.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that optimization-based jailbreak attacks are significantly more effective when guided by actual output harmfulness rather than token-level compliance proxies.

security.title: SAFE-Mem: Secure Agentic Memory with Fine-Grained Authority and Governance-Aware Retrieval

summary.tldr: SAFE-Mem is a memory governance framework for LLM agents that uses fine-grained claim annotation and governance-aware retrieval to block unauthorized memory influence while maintaining high accuracy.
key_points: Annotates atomic claims with three specific governance labels: kind, authority, and scope to control permitted usage.
Constructs a governance-enabled memory graph linking source sentences, claims, and entities for provenance tracking.
Implements governance-aware retrieval to evaluate query requirements against claim permissions before memory injection.
Reduces attack success rates by at least 77% compared to the strongest memory defense baselines while improving answer accuracy by up to 15% on MPBench and LoCoMo benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents untrusted external data from masquerading as authorized system policies or user permissions in long-term LLM agent memory without degrading normal conversational utility.

security.title: Identify, Classify, Act: Per-Instruction Controlled Compliance for LLMs over External Data

summary.tldr: EDIC introduces a per-instruction credit attribution framework using a generative judge trained via SFT and GRPO to resolve the tension between safety and utility in LLMs handling external data.
key_points: Formalizes External-Data Instruction Classification to execute an identify-classify-act decision for each directive interleaved in external documents or tool returns.
Uses a scene-grounded data pipeline with counterfactual filtering to mix beneficial and harmful instructions for training.
Employs a generative judge refined with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to generate separate rewards that penalize harmful compliance while encouraging beneficial compliance.
Outperforms prior defenses on Qwen3-4B, increasing harmful-instruction rejection by up to 7.7% and boosting Arena-Hard-Auto utility by 12.5%.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the compromise between over-refusal and over-compliance by enabling fine-grained, instruction-level control over prompt injections in external data.

security.title: Stealthy Poisoning Attacks via Reused KV Cache of Reasoning

summary.tldr: R2ECAP is a novel black-box attack that poisons LLM reasoning KV caches via standard chat interactions, outperforming white-box methods while evading detection.
key_points: R2ECAP uses a two-trace construct: a preceding trace that steers the model toward an adversarial target, and a retained trace that carries the target into the cached state.
The attack exploits residual adversarial influence preserved in the retained trace's KV cache, which persists even after discarding the preceding trace and its cache entries.
R2ECAP achieves up to a 79% attack success rate (ASR) on open-weight LLMs, outperforming the white-box HijackKV attack in 8 out of 9 resource-constrained settings.
The attack demonstrated a 46% ASR in a realistic reasoning-trace retrieval setup and maintained high stealth, with only 1% of retained responses flagged by a standard prompt injection detector.
summary.why_it_matters: Systems optimizing LLM inference by caching and reusing reasoning traces are vulnerable to persistent, stealthy manipulation entirely through public chat interfaces.

security.title: AI Agents - You Can’t Govern What You Can’t Discover

summary.tldr: The rapid enterprise adoption of agentic AI has heightened data leakage and over-privileging risks, while organizations lack proven solutions to discover and govern these agents.
key_points: Enterprise AI deployment is rapidly shifting from foundational Generative AI to autonomous agentic AI.
The proliferation of AI agents increases organizational risks related to unauthorized data leakage and excessive permission assignments.
Current enterprise security architectures lack proven tools and guardrails to properly discover and govern active AI agents.
summary.why_it_matters: Organizations cannot implement security guardrails or prevent data exposure without first establishing comprehensive visibility over deployed AI agents.

summary.tldr: Researchers developed an adaptive CAPTCHA solver using a confidence-based router between YOLOv8 and an open-weight VLM, allowing the system to learn new CAPTCHA classes autonomously from screenshots without human annotation or DOM access.
key_points: Operates entirely via OS-level inputs and screenshots, achieving 85.4% overall and 84.2% macro accuracy across 16 classes.
Combines a specialized YOLOv8 detector for high-speed inference with an open-weight VLM for handling low-confidence or novel inputs.
Uses VLM outputs as pseudo-labels to train the detector on unseen categories after only one or two encounters.
Recovers automatically from adversarial image perturbations designed to zero out detector accuracy using a ~70%-accurate VLM teacher in a simulated year-long arms race.
summary.why_it_matters: Visual CAPTCHAs relying on static defense assumptions fail against adaptive agents that continuously self-improve and recover from perturbations without human intervention.

infra.title: Introducing TorchNeuron: Native PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium

summary.tldr: AWS and PyTorch announced TorchNeuron, a native, open-source PyTorch backend enabling direct execution, compilation, and profiling on AWS Trainium2 and Trainium3 chips using standard PyTorch APIs.
key_points: Integrates via PyTorch extension points, using PrivateUse1 for hardware registration and support for the torch.accelerator API to enable device switching via .to('neuron').
Supports both eager execution (including an adaptive eager mode) and torch.compile via setting the backend to 'neuron'.
Allows custom hardware kernel development through the Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI).
Integrates with standard PyTorch ecosystem APIs including torch.nn, torch.autocast, torch.distributed, and torch.profiler (via Neuron Explorer).
Releasing as open source under Apache 2.0 at github.com/aws-neuron/torch-neuronx as a public Beta on Oct. 20.
summary.why_it_matters: Developers can run, optimize, and scale PyTorch models on AWS Trainium hardware without altering existing workflow code or leaving the standard PyTorch ecosystem.

infra.title: Inside Prometheus: Meta’s Journey to a Gigawatt-Scale Supercluster

summary.tldr: Meta details its Prometheus supercluster in New Albany, Ohio, which powered the Muse Wonder model training and aims to scale to roughly one million GPUs.
key_points: Achieved over 85% goodput during pre-training and over 90% goodput for reinforcement learning of Muse Wonder, with post-fix wall-clock mean time between interruptions (MTBI) exceeding 54k GPU hours.
Deploys NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 (Catalina) featuring the Ariel variant, a two-rack configuration of 36 GPUs per rack forming a unified 72-GPU NVLink domain on the Open Rack V3 structure.
Pairs each NVIDIA Blackwell GPU with an NVIDIA Grace CPU (1:1 ratio) and 2x NVIDIA ConnectX-7 400G NICs to deliver 800G scale-out I/O per GPU.
Utilizes a hybrid footprint of traditional, AI-optimized, and rapid deployment data center structures with closed-loop liquid cooling, with plans to integrate NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 platforms.
summary.why_it_matters: The architectural and network design of Prometheus allows hundreds of thousands of distributed GPUs to operate efficiently as a single machine, enabling the training of larger foundational models with longer context windows.

summary.tldr: Anthropic is committing 5% of its shares to a new wholly-owned LLC, the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, to support public benefit initiatives as the company grows.
key_points: Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic's shares will be committed immediately, with an optional 2% added per 50% increase in company value above a set baseline.
The Public Benefit Fund is structured as a wholly-owned LLC rather than a 501(c)(3) to allow flexibility across different giving formats, excluding lobbying and political contributions.
Combined with co-founder equity pledges (80%) and an employee equity match program, roughly 20% of Anthropic shares are currently dedicated to public benefit.
The fund will support initiatives such as non-profit donations, direct population distributions, and addressing AI labor market impacts, building on $200 million already committed to labor research.
summary.why_it_matters: The structure dynamically ties Anthropic's corporate valuation growth to an increasing percentage of equity allocated directly for broad public benefit initiatives.
